# QS-PROC-04 Shot peening coverage (P1)
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-IH01

Scope
- This quality specification describes requirements, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for shot peening coverage applied to components processed on line P1-L3 in Plant P1 using EQ-P1-L3-IH01. It applies to all production and rework parts that call out shot peening coverage control in the part drawing, purchase order, or process route. Related documents: ECN-2026-029, SB-1026, SOP-P1-L3-05.

Background and intent
- Shot peening is used to impart controlled compressive residual stress and to improve fatigue life. This specification defines acceptance criteria, establishes inspection methods that are reproducible on the plant floor, and prescribes handling for observed nonconformance. The intent is to ensure consistent peening across part families processed at line P1-L3, with traceability and records that support root cause analysis and corrective action when required.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Description | Responsible |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| Process control | Shot peening parameters shall be set and recorded per the applicable process sheet and SOP-P1-L3-05. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P1-L3-IH01) is 79 L/min. | Process engineer / Operator |
| Coverage documentation | Each peened part shall have a coverage inspection record completed and attached to the lot traveler. Coverage areas and exceptions shall be annotated. | Inspector |
| Media condition | Media lot identifier and media condition verification shall be recorded on the media log prior to production. | Maintenance / Quality |
| Equipment status | Equipment deviations that may affect peening uniformity shall be logged and held out of service until cleared. | Maintenance |
| Traceability | Part numbers, heat numbers, lot identifiers, operator initials, and shift identifier shall be recorded in the process record for each lot. | Operator / Quality |

Inspection method
- Visual sampling and documented measurement shall be used to verify peening coverage. Inspectors shall follow SOP-P1-L3-05 for detailed inspection steps and use calibrated tools listed in SB-1026. Use the following floor-level method to assess coverage:
  - Identify coverage zones per the part drawing and mark on the inspection form.
  - For each coverage zone, perform a surface appearance assessment per the acceptance criteria referenced in ECN-2026-029 and record as acceptable or not acceptable.
  - Capture a photographic record of representative zones for each lot and attach to the lot traveler.
- Rationale: Visual assessment combined with photographic evidence provides repeatable verification that can be reviewed during audits and correlates with fatigue performance when performed per the referenced engineering change and specification documents.
- Examples:
  - Example A: For a multi-feature component with overlapping arcs and flat faces, document inspection for each face and each arc, with photos showing boundary marks.
  - Example B: For a tubular configuration, document inspection on the inner bore and both external surfaces, noting any shadowed areas and corrective action taken to achieve coverage.

Calibration and tools
- Use only inspection tools and gauges referenced in SB-1026. Ensure tools are within calibration status prior to inspection. If tool calibration status is unknown, the lot shall be held pending verification.

Records to keep
- Lot traveler with completed coverage inspection form (attached).
- Photographic evidence files stored in the electronic process archive and referenced on the lot traveler.
- Media lot and condition log from the media storage area.
- Equipment status log for EQ-P1-L3-IH01 during the lot run.
- Calibration certificates for inspection tools used (as referenced in SB-1026).
- Any deviation reports or nonconformance records generated during the lot.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification: Any part or zone failing coverage inspection shall be segregated and tagged as nonconforming. The tag shall reference the lot traveler and inspection record.
- Containment: The affected lot shall be quarantined and production held until disposition is approved by Quality.
- Disposition options:
  - Rework: If re-peening is selected, document corrective actions to address root cause and perform a follow-up inspection per SOP-P1-L3-05. Record media and equipment checks performed prior to rework.
  - Use-as-is with concession: If allowed by the engineering authority under ECN-2026-029, a formal concession shall be recorded and attached to the lot traveler.
  - Scrapping: If neither rework nor concession is acceptable, the lot shall be scrapped per plant scrap procedure and documented.
- Root cause and corrective action: Perform root cause analysis using available records (equipment logs, media logs, operator notes). Document corrective actions and preventive measures in the nonconformance report. Link corrective action to the maintenance work order or engineering change as applicable.

Step rationale
- Segregation and documentation preserve traceability and allow retrospective analysis. Photographs and media logs provide objective evidence of process performance. Referencing ECN-2026-029 ensures any approved deviations or design-specific acceptance criteria are applied consistently. SOP-P1-L3-05 contains the operative floor procedures to ensure inspections are repeatable and auditable.

Audit and review
- Quality shall perform periodic reviews of coverage inspection records and nonconformance trends. Findings that indicate systemic issues require escalation to the process owner and may trigger an engineering review per ECN-2026-029.

References
- ECN-2026-029
- SB-1026
- SOP-P1-L3-05

Distribution and retention
- Retain coverage inspection records and associated attachments as specified in the plant document retention policy. Records shall be available for review during internal and external audits.
